{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The truck would not start in the morning. She heard him trying it from the kitchen, the engine turning over and catching and dying, turning over and catching and dying, and then a long silence in which she pictured him sitting with his hands on the wheel, looking at nothing.

She poured a second cup and carried it out.

He had the hood up by then. The frost had not come off the grass yet, and her boots left dark prints across the yard. He took the cup without looking at her and drank from it and set it on the fender.

"Battery," he said.

"There's the tractor."

"I know there's the tractor."

She waited. He wiped his hands on his jeans, though they were not dirty yet.

"He kept the cables in the barn," she said. "Second stall. Same place."

He looked at her then, briefly, and she saw him decide not to ask how she knew that he knew. He went across to the barn and she stood in the cold and watched the door swing on the hinge that had needed oiling for a year. When he came back he had the cables over his shoulder and something else in his hand, small, that he turned once and put in his pocket without showing her.

The tractor started on the first try. It always had.

He got the truck going and let it run and stood beside it in the exhaust.

"The well," he said. "I could look at it. Before I go."

"It's November."

"I know what month it is."

She picked up the cup from the fender. It was cold again.

"All right," she said. "Look at it.""}
